text_blocks.snippet: The flu typically lasts for 5 to 7 days. However, some people may experience symptoms for up to 2 weeks.

list.title: Day 1-3:
list.snippet: Symptoms usually appear gradually, including fever, chills, body aches, fatigue, and a runny nose.

list.title: Day 4-7:
list.snippet: Symptoms may peak and become more severe, with a persistent cough, sore throat, and congestion.

list.title: Day 8-14:
list.snippet: Symptoms gradually improve, but fatigue and a cough may linger for several more days.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that the duration of the flu can vary depending on factors such as:

list.title: Age:
list.snippet: Children and older adults may experience more severe symptoms and a longer recovery time.

list.title: Underlying health conditions:
list.snippet: People with weakened immune systems or chronic conditions may be more susceptible to complications and a prolonged illness.

list.title: Type of flu virus:
list.snippet: Different strains of the flu virus can have different durations and severities.

text_blocks.snippet: If your symptoms worsen or do not improve after 7 days, it is recommended to seek medical attention.
